anchors.quote: Conditionally treat indices from col through n-1 as a finite search domain. Mark an index i exactly when abs(rows[i][col]) is at least every active-column candidate value and is strictly greater than each value at an earlier index in the domain, thereby specifying Python max's first-index tie behavior. Use Grover-style search only to propose the uniquely marked pivot.

Encode col, candidate indices, and the dynamically updated binary64 values rows[i][col]. A reversible oracle must exactly implement the relevant Python-compatible absolute-value, comparison, equality, and first-index tie semantics. Coherent loading, signed-zero behavior, intermediate nonfinite-state behavior, ancilla cleanup, and all gate and workspace costs remain unresolved.

Measure a proposed index and classically verify that it equals Python's first-index argmax under abs(rows[i][col]). On failed verification, unsuccessful search, or inability to certify the result, execute the original classical max expression. Preserve the zero-pivot check, row swap, elimination order, back substitution, overflow behavior, and report construction unchanged.
Validated inputs begin as finite binary64 values, while the candidate consumes dynamically updated elimination state.

binding.rationale: The concrete predicate remains the initial >=-all and >-earlier rule for absolute pivot magnitudes. The lexical observations added dependency discussion, but no finite-state guard or nonfinite comparison correction is stated. Nonfinite semantics remain an unresolved obligation. Check the same literal local relation with guard True, while preserving the separately declared verification/fallback and unjudged whole-task semantics.

interpretations.meaning: Candidate magnitude is >= every active magnitude and > each earlier active magnitude.
interpretations.expression: all(values[i] >= values[k] for k in indices) and all(values[i] > values[j] for j in indices if j < i)
